newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australian Senate passes revamped pension tax.
newsitem.headline: Australian Senate passes revamped pension tax.

text.p: The Australian parliament's upper house Senate on Monday approved a government move to increase the tax on contributions to pension fund savings for high-income earners.

The Senate passed the A$500 million-a-year measure after it was amended to remove anomalies that might inadvertently catch low-income earners and to exempt workers who received special payments, such as termination payouts.
Prime Minister John Howard's Liberal-National government introduced the move to levy up to an extra 15 percent tax on top of the existing 15 percent tax on pension, or superannuation, contributions.
Under the new scheme, taxpayers pay an extra one percentage point in tax for each A$1,000 of salary over A$70,000 a year, up to a maximum of 15 percent extra.
The Senate also passed an amendment calling the new charge a tax, despite the government's insistence it is a surcharge.
The amended name is certain to be overturned in the government-controlled lower house, the House of Representatives, when it considers the Senate changes.
Howard's coalition campaigned on a policy of no new taxes or tax increases ahead of the March, 1996, election win which saw it oust the 13-year Labor administration.
However, the other amendments are likely to remain.
